deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is Schatten-class theory (Grothendieck writes L^p(H) for what is now S_p, the operators A with tr|A|^p < ∞). The previous page proves a convergence criterion. Proposition 1: hermitian H_i → H_0 in S_p if and only if (1) ||H_i||_p → ||H_0||_p, or merely limsup ||H_i||_p ≤ ||H_0||_p; and (2) for every isolated spectral value λ of H_0, the spectral pieces of H_i in a small window [λ−α, λ+α] eventually have the same finite dimension as that of H_0 and converge to it. Corollary 1 restates this as: H_i → H_0 in S_p if and only if ||H_i||_p → ||H_0||_p and H_i → H_0 in operator norm. Corollary 2: A ↦ |A|^r is continuous from S_p to S_{p/r}.

This page finishes the proof of Corollary 2. The map factors as A ↦ A*A, continuous S_p → S_{p/2}, followed by H ↦ H^{r/2} from the positive cone S^+_{p/2} into S_{p/r}. For the second map one checks the two conditions of Prop. 1:
- Condition 1 is trivial, since ||H^{r/2}||_{p/r}^{p/r} = tr H^{p/2}, so norms converge.
- Condition 2 reduces to finite dimension. On a fixed spectral window, finite-rank positive operators Σ_{i≤n} λ_i a_i⊗a_i converge (λ_i → λ_i^(0), a_i → a_i^(0)). Then Σ λ_i^{r/2} a_i⊗a_i converges too, by continuity of the finite-dimensional functional calculus.

Remark 1 (partly illegible). For 1<p≤2 (the bound written may be 'r ≤ 2' or 'p ≤ 2'), a sequence of hermitians H_k converges in S_p if and only if it converges weakly and the norms converge. This is the Radon–Riesz / Kadec–Klee property; the parenthesis seems to say it follows from the preceding results. He then asks: is this true for all p < ∞? Is S_p uniformly convex?

Remark 2. Fix H, K ≥ 0. Is r ↦ || |H^r − K^r|^{1/r} ||_p an increasing function of r? He notes it would suffice to know the case r < 1, i.e. || |H^r − K^r|^{1/r} ||_p ≤ ||H − K||_p. This reduction is correct: for r1 < r2, put A = H^{r2}, B = K^{r2}, s = r1/r2 < 1, and apply the r<1 case to A, B, s. He adds that this would sharpen Corollary 1/2, turning continuity of H ↦ H^r into an explicit Hölder-type modulus.

The next page moves to Gelfand/approximation numbers ρ_n of operators between Banach spaces. It proves Ky Fan–Weyl type inequalities ρ_{m+n−1}(vu) ≤ ρ_m ρ_n and ρ_{m+n−1}(u+v) ≤ ρ_m + ρ_n, and asks about individual bounds for eigenvalues.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The reduction in Remark 2 to r<1 is correct by reparametrisation (A=H^{r2}, s=r1/r2).
The 'finite dimension' argument for condition 2 is only sketched ('......'). It needs uniform control of the spectral windows, which Prop. 1 provides.
Remark 1's hypothesis is ambiguous in the image ('r ≤ 2' vs '1<p≤2'). As a statement about S_p, the Kadec–Klee property holds for every 1 ≤ p < ∞, including the non-uniformly-convex case p=1.

ideas.what: Continuity of A ↦ |A|^r from S_p to S_{p/r}, via norm convergence plus spectral convergence
ideas.modern_name: Continuity of functional calculus on Schatten ideals; Grümm-type convergence theorem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; convergence criterion of the form 'norm convergence + weak/strong convergence implies S_p convergence' credited to H. Grümm (1973), see B. Simon, Trace Ideals
ideas.where_published: Not in Produits tensoriels topologiques as far as I know; unsure

ideas.what: Question: does weak convergence plus convergence of norms imply S_p-norm convergence for all p<∞; is S_p uniformly convex?
ideas.modern_name: Kadec–Klee (Radon–Riesz) property of Schatten classes; uniform convexity of S_p
ideas.usually_credited_to: Uniform convexity: Dixmier (1953) and C. McCarthy (1967, Clarkson–McCarthy inequalities). Kadec–Klee for S_1: Arazy (1981) and Simon (1981)

ideas.what: Question: is || |H^r−K^r|^{1/r} ||_p increasing in r, equivalently || |H^r−K^r|^{1/r} ||_p ≤ ||H−K||_p for 0<r<1?
ideas.modern_name: Operator-Hölder inequality for t^r in Schatten / unitarily invariant norms (Powers–Størmer type)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Powers–Størmer (1970, case r=1/2, p=1); Birman–Koplienko–Solomyak (1975); Ando (1988, general unitarily invariant norms, operator monotone f); Aleksandrov–Peller

missed.claim: In 1953 Grothendieck explicitly formulated the Schatten-norm Hölder inequality || |H^r−K^r|^{1/r} ||_p ≤ ||H−K||_p for positive H, K and 0<r<1. He also observed that it is equivalent to monotonicity in r. It was proved only by Birman–Koplienko–Solomyak (1975) and generalised by Ando (1988); his early formulation of this question appears unrecorded.
missed.quote: Est-ce que S_p ‖H^r−K^r‖^{1/r} est fonction croissante de r (H hermitien positif)? — Il suffirait de le savoir pour r<1 i.e. ‖(H^r−K^r)^{1/r}‖ ≤ ‖H−K‖
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only historical priority for a question, not a result. The inequality is now standard, so it is of no mathematical novelty today.

missed.claim: He asks whether the Kadec–Klee property (weak convergence plus norm convergence implies strong convergence) holds in S_p for all p<∞, and links it to uniform convexity. This was answered later: McCarthy (1967) for 1<p<∞, Arazy and Simon (1981) for p=1.
missed.quote: Est-ce vrai si p < ∞ ? Uniforme convexité de L^p ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical only; the question is settled.

deep.surprise_reason: The page completes a routine continuity proof. It then poses two natural questions on Schatten classes, both later resolved by others (Kadec–Klee/uniform convexity; the Birman–Koplienko–Solomyak/Ando operator-Hölder inequality). Grothendieck's 1953 formulation predates those results by 15–35 years, which is a modest historical point but contains no new mathematics.
